lines.text: Why will you never see a square window on a plane?
The very first jet airliner, back in the fifties, had big, nearly square windows, so passengers could watch the world go by.
Vik bets a week of desserts that round windows are just for looks.
But this jet flew higher than any airliner before, so every single flight pumped the cabin up like a balloon, and let it back down again.
Within two years, two of them broke apart in the sky.
So engineers sank a whole plane in a giant water tank and pumped it up and down, again and again, thousands of times.
Until it burst, and the crack started at a sharp corner.
That's when Gus cuts a square hole and a round hole in paper, and pulls.
The square tears at the corner. The round one holds.
You see, a sharp corner squeezes all the stress into one tiny point, but a smooth curve spreads it gently all the way around.
So every airliner built since then has rounded windows.
And Vik's square brownie? It cracks right at the corner.
So next time you fly, look out and ask…
